text.original: महाराष्ट्र के जिऱा चन्द्रऩुर के गोववंदऩुर ताम्र खननि प्राजतत के आसऩास ताम्र तथा उससे िुडे स्वणण खननिन के ऺेत्रों की स्थाऩना हेतु अन्द्वेषण ऩर प्रनतवेदन (ऩी-II स्तर) (धयातर ऩत्रक सं ५५ऩी/११ के बाग) ऺेत्रकार २००७-२००८ तथा २००८-२००९ (भद कोड सं. ०.३९/एभआईऩी/सीआय/भहा./२००७/०१२) व्दाया आर.एच. चव्हाण, कननष्ट्ठ भूवैऻाननक, के.सी. महाऩात्र, वररष्ट्ठ भूवैऻाननक (ऩीटी), एम. महािन, कननष्ट्ठ भूवैऻाननक (ऩीटी), एस.ऩी. धनवविय, वररष्ट्ठ भूवैऻाननक, बी.वी. श्रीरामा, कननष्ट्ठ भूभौनतकीववद सारांश ताम्र खननजन के ननरूऩण ऺेत्र के उद्देश्म से वषा २००७-२००९ के दौयान १:२,००० ऩैभाने ऩय ०.५ वगा ककरोभीटय ऺेत्र का ववस्तृत भानचचत्रण गोववंदऩुय तथा फोथरी ऺेत्र के आसऩास ककमा गमा, जजसभें क्रभफद्ध नभूनें ५१६ भृदा प्रनतदशी, ५५ संस्तय शैर प्रनतदशी, ११ गता प्रनतदशी तथा १० शैरकीम प्रनतदशी ऩय कामा ककमा गमा | इस गवेषण ऺेत्र भें ऩेनगंगा सभूह के अवसादी आवयण शैरों के साथ आककामन आधायी शैरें शाशभर हैं । मह आधायी शैरें भेटाऩेराइटों के साथ फेंगऩार नाइस व्दाया प्रनतननचधत्व कयते हैं जो कक ऩेग्भेटाइट, क्वाटाज तथा एवऩडोट शशयाओं व्दाया अन्तवेचधत हैं । गोववंदऩुय ऩुयाने कामा ऺेत्र भें भेटाऩेराइटों, क्वाटाज, अभ्रक शशस्ट के अन्तवेधन से भेराकाइट धब्फों के साथ क्वाटाज शशयाओं को भानचचबत्रत ककमा था । ऩुयाने कामा ऺेत्र भें औय उसके आसऩास क्वाटाज टूयभैरीन ऩट्टिमों के कुछेक छोटे ववमुक्त दृश्मांश बी देखे गए हैं । उत्तय-दक्षऺण प्रवणता की खननजीकृत क्वाटाज शशया उत्तयऩूवा की ओय अल्ऩ अवनभन ननम्न ननभज्जन (१२.१५) के साथ स्ऩष्ट रूऩ से वरननत है । ववकीणान के रूऩ भें, फोथरी सल्पाइड ( चाल्कोऩामयाइट, फोनााइट तथा ऩामयाइट) शसशरसीकृत ऺेत्रों भें देखा गमा है । शसशरसीकृत ऺेत्र भें भेराकाइट ऩऩाटी व्दाया ताम्र खननजन ट्टदखाई देती है जो कक फेंगऩार नाइस के बीतय भेटाऩेराइट के ऩरयऺेत्र को ऩरयसीशभत कयती है तथा इनकी प्रवणता उत्तय-दक्षऺण तथा उत्तय-उत्तयऩूवा – दक्षऺण-दक्षऺणऩजश्चभ की ओय भ्रंश ऺेत्रों की ओय अशबस्थावऩत है । ऺेत्रकार वषा २००८-२००९ भें ताम्र खननजन के ववऺेऩण ऩध्दनत को जानने

text.original: ककमा गमा तथा २५ भृदा नभूनों भें (३००० ऩीऩीएभ से ६००० ऩीऩीएभ तक) आधाय धातु का ऩता रगामा गमा | वताभान ऺेत्रकार के दौयान खननजन के भूर को सभझने के शरए ववस्तृत ऩेट्रोभाइक्रोस्कोऩी अध्ममन ककमा गमा । अध्ममन ऺेत्र भें, मंगय खननजन अऩरूवऩत क्वार्टाज शशयाएं / यीप के साथ एजम्पफोराइट, पाइब्रोराइट, भाइरोनाइट तथा क्वार्टाज-क्रोयाइट भाइरोनाइट मे उऩजस्थत प्रभुख शैर प्रकाय हैं । इस ऺेत्र भें भाइरोनाइट तथा क्वार्टाज यीप भें तीव्र भाइरोनीकयण तथा ववखंडन से मह ऩता चरता है कक महां बंगुस्तन्म अऩरूऩण हुआ है । जरोढक अऩरूवऩत क्वार्टाज शशयाएं/ यीप व्दाया सल्पाइड खननजन जैसे ऩामयाइट, चाल्को ऩामयाइट, कोवेराइट तथा ऩेक्साइट आनतथेम / ऩयऩोषी हैं । इस ऺेत्र भें खननजन की तीन शबन्न शबन्न प्रावस्था ऩाई जाती हैं । खननजन की इन सबी प्रावस्थाओं को अऩरूऩण की ववशबन्न अवस्थाओं तथा क्वार्टाज यीप / शशया अन्तवेधन के साथ सह-सम्फद्ध ककमा जा सकता है । सूक्ष्भदशी व्दाया क्वार्टाज भें संस्तयों का अवरोकन कयने से मह ऩता चरता है कक क्वार्टाज फहुभूल्म शसशरका-सभृध्द जरोश्भ द्रव्म से अवऺेवऩत है । शसशरका- सभृध्द जरो भें सल्पाइड खननजन ऩामा जाता है । ऺेत्रकार २००७-०८ भें भहायाष्ट्र के जजरा चन्द्रऩुय के गोववंदऩुय खण्ड भें ०.८५ वगा ककरोभीटय के ऺेत्रपर भें बूबौनतकी सवेऺण भें ननमोजजत एसऩी, चुम्फकीम, प्रनतयोधक के साथ आईऩी तकनीक (िेडडएन्ट ऐये), वट्टटाकर इरैजक्ट्रकर साउडडंग तथा डाइऩोर - डाइऩोर व्दाया ककमा गमा ।

text.original: REPORT ON INVESTIGATION FOR ESTABLISHING ZONES OF COPPER AND ASSOCIATED GOLD MINERALISATION AROUND GOVINDPUR COPPER PROSPECT, CHANDRAPUR DISTRICT, MAHARASHTRA (P-II STAGE) (PART OF TOPOSHEET NO. 55P/11) Field Seasons 2007-08 and 2008-2009 (Item Code No. 039/MIP/CR/MH/2007/012) By R.H. Chavhan, Jr. Geologist, K. C. Mahapatra, Sr. Geologist (PT), M. Mahajan, Jr. Geologist (PT), S.P. Dhanvijay, Sr. Geologist B.V. Srirama, Jr. Geophysicist PART-I ABSTRACT Detailed mapping of 0.5 sq km area on 1:2,000 scale, systematic sampling, 535 soil samples, 90 bed rock samples, 5 nos. of pit samples and 25 petrological samples, in grid pattern around Govindpur and Bothli areas were carried out during 2007-09 with the objective to delineate zones of Copper mineralisation. The explored area comprises Archaean basement rocks with sedimentary cover rocks of Penganga Group. The basement rocks are represented by Bengpal gneiss with metapelites, which have been intruded by pegmatite, quartz and epidote veins. Quartz vein with malachite stains intruding metapelites (quartz mica schist) was mapped in Govindpur old working area. A few small isolated outcrop of quartz - tourmaline bands are also seen in and around old working area. The mineralised quartz vein trending N-S is broadly folded with low plunge (12-15º) towards NE. At Bothli Sulphides (chalcopyrite, Bornite and pyrite), in the form of disseminations, are noticed in the silicified zones. The copper mineralisation is manifested by malachite encrustations in silicified zone, which are confined to enclaves of metapelite within Bengpal gneiss and have been emplaced along N-S and NNE-SSW trending fault zones. A total of 325 soil samples were collected in grid pattern 100m x 25m in order to know the dispersion pattern of copper mineralisation during field season 2008-09. Both soil and bed rock samples were collected in Govindpur and Bothli areas in grid pattern (100 x 25). The analytical values in soil samples range from 20 ppm to 0.10% Cu, <10 to 125 ppm Pb, 20 to 500 ppm Zn whereas the values range from 0.77% 3.15% Cu, <10 to 0.18% Pb and <10 to 100 ppm Zn for bed rock samples.

text.original: Soil samples (6 nos) collected near Govindpur old working, show anomalous zone indicates Cu values range from 0.10% to 0.64% of strike length 125m. Stream sediments samples collected from the study area show cu values range from 12 ppm to 116 ppm , Pb from 9 ppm to 75 ppm , Zn from 17 ppm to 62 ppm, Co from 7ppm to 178ppm, Ni from 17ppm to 146 ppm, and Au values <100ppb. In Govindpur area, the analytical values of the pits/trenches samples shows copper values range from <100 ppm to 895 ppm, Pb values from 7 ppm to 41 ppm, Zn from 32 ppm to 169, Co from 20 ppm to 75 ppm, Ni from 30 ppm to 123 ppm, Au values of 4 pits/trenches ranging from 100 ppb to 140 ppb while others 2 pits/trenches shows Au values <100 ppb. In Bothli area, the analytical values of the pits/trenches samples range from 10 ppm to 225 ppm Cu, 10 ppm to 20 ppm Pb, 100 ppm to, 125 ppm Zn, 40 ppm to 75 ppm Co, <10 pm to 10 pm Ni, 2 ppm to 10 ppm As while Au is <100 ppb and for bed rock samples from <10 ppm to 0.25% Cu, <10 ppm to 60 ppm Pb, <10 ppm to 175 ppm Zn, 40 ppm to 275 ppm Co, <10 ppm to 20 ppm Ni, <1 ppm to 10 ppm As, and Au values <100 ppb to 160 ppb. The cold extraction method have been adopted and used for determination of Cu% and other elements in ppm in the soil as well in the stream sediments samples. The total 78 soil samples were analysed and detected base metal in 25 soil samples (ranges from 3,000 ppm to 6,000 ppm). During the current field season detailed petromicroscopic studies has been carried out to understand the origin of mineralization. The main rock types present in study area are quartz-chlorite mylonite, quartz-fibrolite mylonite, garnetiferous quartz monzonite, and amphibolites with younger mineralized sheared quartz veins/reef. Intense mylonitisation and brecciation in mylonite and quartz vein/reef indicates brittle-ductile shearing occurred in the area. The sulphide mineralization viz., pyrite, chalcopyrite, covellite and paxite are hosted by hydrothermal sheared quartz veins/reef. Three distinct phases of mineralization are present in the area. All these phases of mineralization can be correlated with different stages of shearing and quartz reef/vein intrusion. The zoning in quartz observed under microscope suggests that quartz precipitated from a polygenic silica-rich hydrothermal fluid. Silica-rich hydrothermal fluid carries the sulphide mineralization. Geophysical surveys employing SP, Magnetic, resistivity cum IP techniques (Gradient Array), Vertical electrical sounding and Dipole-dipole were conducted over an area of 0.85 Sq km in Govindpur block of Chandrapur District of Maharashtra in FS 2007-08

Southerly flowing Upasa nala and Gondri nadi form the tributaries of Wainganga River. Ghodazhari canal system irrigates the paddy field in this area. The area around Bothli in general is a flat terrain except for two hills comprising younger sedimentary rocks (equivalent to Vindhyans) in the eastern and other in western parts of the area. The area is drained by Gondri Nadi, east of Bothli and also by number of southeasterly nalas. Water level in the wells range from 3 to 9m in depth from surface. 1.4 Climate and vegetation: The climatic conditions in the areas are extreme both in summer and winter. In summer temperature ranges from 380 to 450C while during winter it drops to a minimum of 120C. The average rainfall in the area is about 125 cm, much of which precipitated between July and August. The area is thickly forested by open and bushy, mixed open forest comprises of Bhramapuri and Pendhri reserved forest to the west and north of Govindpur respectively. text.original: 5 2.0 GEOLOGY 2.1 Regional Geology The studied area “Govindpur Copper Prospect” is located in the western part of Bastar craton and exposes basement gneisses belonging to the Bengpal Group with enclaves of older metapelites and zones of silicification. The gneisses are overlain by sandstone and quartzite equated to Penganga Group. Penganga sandstone is best exposed at 2.5 km ENE of Bothli village. It occurs as outlier trending NNW-SSE with gentle dip of 100 to 350 towards NE. At some places strike varies E-W with northerly dip of 150 to 250. Penganga sandstone is hard, compact, medium to fine grained, brown whitish yellow or buff coloured rock due to presence of ferruginous cementing material. It mainly comprises of grit and arkose. The area shows lineaments trending NW-SE and NNE-SSW direction. The mineralisation is essentially controlled by NS and NNE-SSW trending lineaments with silicified sheared quartz veins/reef. The silicified sheared quartz vein occurred in the form of ridges at various places in the area, viz: the ridge 1.5 km north of Sonoli, 2 km south of Motegaon and near Lawari village, are associated with copper mineralisation, malachite encrustation, pyrite, chalcopyrite and a few grains of covellite. The other sheared quartz veins which are devoid of any mineralisation have been noticed about 5 km southwest of Talodhi and about 4 km east of Nander village trending NW and at some places trend varies from NS to NE-SW with dip varying from 350 to 800 towards west. In Govindpur and Bothli blocks, malachite encrustation is seen in quartz veins with disseminated fine specks of pyrite and chalcopyrite. text.original: 6 Bengpal Group of Archaean age occupies part of the investigation area. It comprises of granite gneisses and migmatite with enclaves of hornblende schist, amphibolites, ultramafic and quartz/pegmatite veins. Bailadila Group of Palaeoproterozoic age (2500-2200 m.y) comprising quartzite, banded haematite quartzite with lenses of iron ores occurs as isolated outcrops in the southern part of the area. Penganga Group (equivalent) of Neoproterozoic age occupies in the northern, northeastern and south western part of the area. Archaean gneiss forms the plain topography in the area while Penganga sandstone and quartzite forms small hillocks and ridges. Most of the area is covered by thick soil. Bengpal Gneissic Group forming the basement for all the overlying lithounits, consists of granite gneiss/pegmatite with enclaves of older metamorphics (metapelites). Bengpal Group of rocks have general NNW-SSE to NW-SE strike with a gentle dip towards NNE or NE direction. The foliations of Archaean gneisses and schists have NW-SE strike but NE-SW trend is also observed. The enclave of metapelites in basement gneisses trend in N350W- S350E with 250 to 500 dip towards SW. The sedimentary rocks resting unconformably on the metamorphics, referable to Penganga Group, show NW-SE strike with a low dips (40 to 100) to NE. Sandstones are medium to fine grained, hard, compact, white to buff coloured having minor secondary quartz veins at places. 2.2 Detailed geology: The brief stratigraphy of the mapped area is as follows Sandstone Penganga Group Neoproterozoic Tourmaline vein Bengal Group Archaean Quartz vein-Silicified zone Amphibolite Quartz monzonite Quartz chlorite schist Granite gneiss

text.original: 10 4.0 Mineralization Mineralisation is noticed in general along the NNW-SSE trending shear zone, which consists of both metallic and non-metallic minerals. The sulphide mineralization is associated with silicified quartz reef/veins and essentially consists of chalcopyrite, pyrite, chalcocite, covellite and malachite. The sulphide mineralisation occur mainly in the form of dissemination, fracture fillings and specks in highly fractured and silicified quartz veins, at places also occur as discrete grains in host rock. The mineralisation is essentially structurally controlled confined to shear opening and fracture. The mineralisation appears to be hydrothermal in origin as indicated by wall rock alteration and nature of its occurrences within the host rock. The mineralisation in the area may be attributed to hydrothermal origin related to the younger granite intrusives into the basement in the vicinity, which is evidenced by numerous pink felspar and quartz veins within the metapelites. The Cu mineralisation in this area displays a distinct structural (fracture planes) and lithological control (altered metapelites) suggesting an epigenetic origin. The sulphide crustification and comb structures noticed along fracture planes of silicified quartz veins and metapelites rock also suggests an epithermal type of mineralisation.

text.original: 13 6.0 Ore Petrography In the study area, sulphide mineralization is hosted by hydrothermal quartz veins. Mineralization occurs as disseminated specks, veinlets comprising of pyrite, chalcopyrite, covellite and paxite. 6.1 Pyrite (FeS2): It occurs as veins, cavity fillings as well as in disseminations (Fig.-11) with euhedral outline and typical pitted nature due to its high hardness. It is light yellow colour with high reflectance and distinct isotropism. 6.2 Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2): It occurs as a minor phase in quartz vein. It is medium grained with pure yellow colour and shows weak anisotropism in greenish grey tints. 6.3 Covellite (CuS): It occurs as lamellae of pure blue coloured (Fig.-12), shows strong pleochroism and extreme anisotropism in orange brown (Fig.-13). 6.4 Paxite (CuAs2): It is fine grained, subidiomorphic, yellow-white in colour with high reflectance and occurs as discrete grains with typical twin lamellae and distinct anisotropism. 6.5 Paragenesis: The ore petrographic studies of the mineralized zones of Govindpur and Bothli blocks shows prominent sulphide mineralization viz., pyrite, chalcopyrite, covellite and paxite along with hematite representing the oxide phase. From the ore petrographic study it is very much evident that at least three generations of mineralization are present in the area. The early phase is marked by chalcopyrite, covellite and paxite in decreasing abundance followed by distinct pyrite in the second phase. Hematite occurs as discrete grains filling cavities and veins forms last phase of mineralization. Chalcopyrite and covellite shows mutual boundary texture indicating their coeval nature. However, paxite occurs as discrete grains with typical twin lamellae and distinct anisotropism. Pyrite shows prominent replacement texture, where it is replacing chalcopyrite. Undigested chalcopyrite is recorded within the pyrite. All these phases of mineralization can be correlated with different stages of shearing and quartz reef/vein intrusion. First phase of mineralization is mainly associated with syn shearing quartz reef intrusion and second as well as third/last phase are associated with post shearing quartz veins.

But remaining part of the high chargeability is associated with high resistivity (Fig.-9) formations of the resistivity values more than 600ohm-m that indicate the mineralisation is highly disseminated. text.original: 17 9.0 Conclusions and Recommendations Detailed geological mapping were carried out in both areas to probe mineralization at depth and its strike continuity in the area. From the data collected by soil samples analysis in Govindpur and Bothli areas of Chandrapur District, it is concluded that the mineralization is restricted in extent without much depth persistence. The mineralization zone in Bothli area has considerable length and width. The quality of the ore is also good. Observation of the trial pits opened in the area indicated that wall rocks are highly altered by hydrothermal agencies as is evident from silicification and Chloritisation of the rock. West of Govindpur, an area of 2km.towards Bothli old working further needs chemical analysis of soil samples, extensive pitting and trenching to know strike continuity of copper ore horizon.  In Govindpur and Bothli block, the main rock types present are quartz- chlorite mylonite, quartz-fibrolite mylonite, garnetiferous quartz monzonite, and amphibolites with younger mineralized sheared quartz reef/vein.  Intense mylonitisation and brecciation in mylonite and quartz vein indicates brittle- ductile shearing occurred in the area.  Development of lenses/ribbons, crushing, granulation and recrystallisation of quartz indicates intense shearing. The zoning in quartz in silicified quartz vein observed under microscope suggests that quartz precipitated from a polygenic silica-rich hydrothermal fluid, which is also the carrier of sulphide mineralization.  The general sulphide mineral assemblage recorded in the area include pyrite, chalcopyrite, covellite and paxite CuAs2) along with hematite representing the oxide phase.  At least three distinct phases of mineralization is recorded based on textural relationship between ore minerals and ore and gangue minerals marked by both sulphide and oxide phases.  All these phases of mineralization can be correlated with different stages of shearing and quartz reef/vein intrusion. First phase of mineralization is mainly associated with syn shearing quartz reef intrusion and second as well as third/last phase are associated with post shearing quartz veins.  Pervasive hydrothermal activity in the area resulted intense wall rock alteration viz, silicification, sericitisation, chloritisation, sausaritization indicating an epithermal to mesothermal nature of mineralization. In Govindpur copper prospect, no gold mineralization is found. Sulphide minerals viz. pyrite, chalcopyrite, covelite, paxite are found but in less concentration.
